body:
> a comment under the scroll_vector declaration in Godot suggests it's in pixels; testing on my end suggests they are pixels independent of screen scaling

Bingo! Wayland uses a concept of "logical pixels", which we then scale. Pretty sure that's what the motion even uses (and even defines). Actually, the fact that we pass that to Godot as-is is a bug IMO, please see #116516.

> I think it's safe to conclude that the scroll vector is in a more precise coordinate system than what it's being interpreted as by Godot.

Indeed, that's what I think too. It was maybe intended to use "fractions of a detent" which are actually, from my understanding, mapped to `InputEventMouseButton::set_factor` with a mouse-wheel button set. That said, I don't think that your solution is the most ideal, as it switches a set of magic numbers for another.

I think that we should simply assume we're working in pixels and use that to manipulate the object 1:1. I've done some limited, testing, but please read https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116499#issuecomment-3936912068 for my observations.
